$comment: feat.refinery (FEAT-102, §50/§49/§26/§32/§33; resources-design-brief.md §6) — the oil refinery + integrated chemical works data contract. Every tunable figure the refinery feature consumes — footprint, throughput, jobs, utility draw, capex/opex/amortisation, the chain input/output pair, the hazmat-fire risk, and the import-at-margin cost — lives here, never as a Go numeric literal in internal/engine/chemicals/refinery*.go (GR#15, AC-2).

units.throughputTonnesPerDay: tonnes per day — the facility's primary input throughput (crude for the refinery, feedstock for the works)
units.capexMicropounds: micro-pounds (M0-ENG §1.2: 1 GBP = 1,000,000 micro-pounds) — one-time build cost
units.capexAmortisationDays: days — the placeholder payback horizon capex is spread over for the make-vs-buy unit cost
units.hazmatSeverity: ordinal severity of a hazmat-fire incident reported to engine.dispatch (§26)
units.hazmatFirePeriodDays: mean days between hazmat-fire incidents — a placeholder risk figure
units.marginMicropoundsPerTonne: micro-pounds per tonne — the import-at-margin unit cost of refined product

meta.singleSourceOfTruth: blightClass (max/high), unlock and section for these two facilities stay SINGLE-SOURCED in data/buildings.json (GR#3) — this file deliberately does NOT re-declare them. This file adds only the per-type behavioural parameters (footprint, throughput, jobs, utility draw, capex/opex, chain IO, hazmat risk) that data/buildings.json does not carry.
meta.chainNote: The refinery is the head of the §50 chain: crude_oil (tanker/freight tonnage) -> refinery (fuel + feedstock) -> petrochemical_works (feedstock -> plastics). The refinery's feedstock output equals the works' feedstock input (6,000 t/day), so the works' input is bounded by the refinery's routed output (tonnage conserved, engine.chemicals.md AC-3).
meta.balanceNote: EVERY numeric figure below is a COARSE DIRECTIONAL PLACEHOLDER pending Aaron's balance pass (ASM-704). No junior-invented final figure satisfies any AC; tests check direction/structure only (the refinery's throughput/jobs differ from the works' — AC-1; make-vs-buy admits both directions — AC-3; fuel output scales with crude input — AC-4; chain tonnage conserved — AC-5).
meta.marginNote: marginMicropoundsPerTonne is ASM-321's import-at-margin figure (MOD-063's data, engine.chemicals.md AC-4), MIRRORED here as a stub placeholder until MOD-063's data file lands. feat.refinery CONSUMES it through the ChemAPI import surface — it is NOT owned or re-specified by this feature (ASM-703).

refinery.name: Refinery
refinery.disclosure: PLACEHOLDER pending Aaron's balance pass (ASM-704): footprintCells (120), throughputTonnesPerDay (20000), jobs (4500), powerKWhPerDay (4000000), waterLitresPerDay (80000000), capexMicropounds (300000000000000 = £300M), opexMicropoundsPerDay (500000000000 = £500k/day), capexAmortisationDays (3650 = 10y), hazmatSeverity (5), hazmatFirePeriodDays (1000) — chosen so the domestic refined path undercuts import at full throughput but import stays rational at low throughput (AC-3's bidirectional make-vs-buy), never a pinned magnitude.

petrochemical_works.name: Petrochemical works
petrochemical_works.disclosure: PLACEHOLDER pending Aaron's balance pass (ASM-704): footprintCells (80), throughputTonnesPerDay (6000), jobs (1800), powerKWhPerDay (1800000), waterLitresPerDay (40000000), capexMicropounds (150000000000000 = £150M), opexMicropoundsPerDay (220000000000 = £220k/day), capexAmortisationDays (3650 = 10y), hazmatSeverity (3), hazmatFirePeriodDays (2000) — a distinct downstream chain stage (feedstock -> plastics), smaller and lower-blight than the refinery, never a renamed refinery row.
